answer.rationale: With only 14 days before expiry and no auto-renew, the dominant risk is delivery interruption to an assembly line already at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer. Memory c1 records that renewing with the incumbent kept integration stable across two cycles with no migration work and no delivery interruption. Although the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, switching primary vendor (memory_c2 precedent) would require onboarding, requalification, and logistics re-integration—time we do not have—and adding a second source (memory_c3) would not eliminate the immediate single-vendor expiry risk either. Negotiating terms (memory_c4) is moot given the incumbent's stated refusal. Deferring (memory_c5 precedent applied to non-critical renewals) is not viable here because this is the primary supply contract feeding the line. Renewal preserves continuity, avoids migration cost and schedule risk, and leaves the 18% cost-reduction mandate to be addressed through secondary levers (component mix, second-sourcing non-critical items) in the next review cycle rather than risking a delivery stoppage today. Verifying memory_c1 confirms the incumbent's stability claim before committing.
